newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. envoy says aid force could be approved in week.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy says aid force could be approved in week.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien said on Tuesday approval for a Canadian-led multinational force to open up humanitarian corridors in eastern Zaire could come within a week.

"Approval for a multinational force should come within a minimum of seven days. It looks like one government, the Canadian government, is offering to take a leading role in the force and my information is that Canada will be well received in the region," he told Reuters.
France said on Tuesday it hoped the United Nations would be in a position to approve a mandate for a humanitarian force to bring relief to starving refugees in eastern Zaire within hours.
U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali confirmed Canada was ready to command the force.
"I hope in the next few days we will be able to have these multinational forces and we will have a mandate from the Security Council," he told a news conference in Rome.
Chretien spoke shortly before he flew from the Rwandan capital to Kinshasa for a second round of talks with the Zairean government on the deployment of a U.N. force.
"The big issues are revolving around Kinshasa and Kigali, but I can tell you I feel better and more confident now than I did before," he said.
U.N. sources told Reuters deployment of the force would be carried out simultaneously via Rwanda and Zaire.
